questions.q: Which stage of the policy cycle involves deciding which issues need to be addressed on a priority basis?
options: Policy monitoring
Prioritising policy
Policy evaluation
Policy implementation
questions.explanation: Prioritising policy means deciding which issues need to be addressed on a priority basis. It comes after problems are identified and before the policy is formulated in detail.
questions.fact: Prioritising Policy: Deciding which issues need to be addressed on priority basis.
questions.hint: The stage's name literally means putting things in order of importance.

questions.q: In a democratic country like India, governance is guided by ___.
options: the constitution, which lays down the framework for governing the nation
the orders of colonial rulers
the decisions of foreign companies
the wishes of a single leader
questions.explanation: In a democracy like India, governance is guided by the constitution, which lays down the framework for governing the nation. This keeps governance within democratic values and rules.
questions.fact: In a democratic country like India, governance is guided by the constitution, which lays down the framework for governing the nation.
questions.hint: It is the country's supreme rulebook.

questions.q: According to the chapter, through a public policy, governments decide what should be done, why, who will do it, and ___.
options: how it will be implemented and how its success will be measured
which citizens will be exempt from all laws
how to cancel future elections
how to avoid all public feedback
questions.explanation: Through a public policy, governments decide what should be done, why it should be done, who will do it, how it will be implemented, and how its success will be measured. The policy is then monitored and evaluated through a feedback loop.
questions.fact: Through this course of action, governments decide what should be done, why it should be done, who will do it, how it will be implemented, and how its success will be measured.
questions.hint: The list runs from 'what' all the way to measuring success.

questions.q: According to the chapter, a robust democracy requires transparent institutions, responsible representatives, and ___.
options: the continuous participation of people in public life
frequent changes of the constitution
the withdrawal of citizens from public affairs
control by a few wealthy families
questions.explanation: In a well-functioning democracy, participating only in elections to form the government is not enough. Transparent institutions, responsible representatives, and the continuous participation of people in public life are all needed.
questions.fact: A robust democracy requires transparent institutions, responsible representatives, and the continuous participation of people in public life.
questions.hint: Democracy needs citizens to stay active beyond election day.

questions.q: With time, the needs, desires, and aspirations of people evolve, creating new challenges to which the government and institutions have to respond.
questions.explanation: The task of governance is always ongoing because people's needs, desires, and aspirations keep evolving. Governments and institutions must respond to these new challenges continuously.
questions.fact: The task of governance is always ongoing. With time, the needs, desires, and aspirations of people also evolve, creating new challenges to which the government and the institutions have to respond.
questions.hint: Change in society keeps governance on its toes.

questions.q: In the Indian tradition, good governance was measured only by the ruler's authority.
questions.explanation: Good governance was measured not only by the ruler's authority but by the peace, prosperity, justice, and well-being in society. The welfare of the people, not the ruler's power, was the true test.
questions.fact: Good governance was measured not only by the ruler's authority but by the peace, prosperity, justice, and well-being in society.
questions.hint: The real measure was the condition of the people.

questions.q: The Ṛigveda refers to the Sabhā and the ___ as important institutions where matters of governance and public welfare were discussed.
questions.explanation: The Ṛigveda refers to the Sabhā and Samiti as important institutions where matters of governance and public welfare were discussed. They show that participative governance has ancient roots in India.
questions.fact: The Ṛigveda refers to the Sabhā and Samiti as important institutions where matters of governance and public welfare were discussed.
questions.hint: It sounds like 'committee'.

questions.q: Governance refers to the way a country, state, city, village, school, or organisation is ___.
questions.explanation: Governance is the way any collective — from a whole country down to a school — is managed. Understanding it helps us know how government impacts our lives.
questions.fact: It refers to the way a country, state, city, village, school, or organisation is managed.
questions.hint: It is what good managers do.

questions.q: The Sengol was placed in India's newly inaugurated ___ building in the year 2023.
questions.explanation: The Sengol, a cultural marker of rulership and good governance, was placed in the newly inaugurated Parliament building in 2023 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, reviving a Chola-era tradition.
questions.fact: The Sengol — a cultural marker of rulership and good governance — was placed in India's newly inaugurated Parliament building in the year 2023 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
questions.hint: It is the building where our lawmakers sit.

questions.q: Arrange these levels of the Khelo Bharat Niti's implementation structure from the national level down to the block level.
questions.explanation: The Union Government sits at the top with the policy framework and funding, followed by states, then districts, and finally blocks where sporting programmes reach the ground. Strengthening the ecosystem from the block to the national level is the Niti's key focus.
questions.fact: Its agencies located at lower vertical levels of states, districts and blocks... 'Strengthening the sporting culture and ecosystem from the block level to the national level is a key focus of the Khelo Bharat Niti 2025'.
questions.hint: Follow the order: nation, then state, then district, then block.

questions.q: Arrange these three in order, from the broadest direction to the most specific action.
questions.explanation: A policy is the broad goal or direction, a programme explains the plan or approach for achieving that goal, and a scheme is the specific action through which the programme is implemented. Policy gives direction, programmes show the path, and schemes are the course of action.
questions.fact: Policy provides direction, programmes provide the plan, and schemes put the plan into action.
questions.hint: Think big goal, then plan, then action on the ground.

questions.q: Arrange these milestones in the evolution of governance in India in the correct chronological order.
orderItems: Kings upheld Rājadharma as their foremost duty
Colonial rulers imposed their own models of governance on India
'Satyamev Jayate' was adopted as the national motto after Independence
The Sengol was placed in the newly inaugurated Parliament building
questions.explanation: The tradition of Rājadharma is ancient, colonial rule came later, 'Satyamev Jayate' was adopted after Independence in 1947, and the Sengol was placed in the new Parliament building in 2023.
questions.fact: Indian tradition viewed governance as a sacred responsibility... colonial rulers forced their own models of governance... after Independence, we have adopted 'Satyamev Jayate'... the Sengol was placed in India's newly inaugurated Parliament building in 2023.
questions.hint: Ancient traditions come first; the year 2023 comes last.

questions.q: Select all whose roles matter for the success of the Khelo Bharat Niti 2025.
options: Families of young sportspersons
Only international sports bodies
Athletes and coaches
Schools and local bodies
questions.explanation: The Niti's success depends on many stakeholders — states, districts, local bodies, schools, coaches, families, and athletes. International sports bodies are not listed among them in the chapter.
questions.fact: Its success depends on many stakeholders — in this case, states, districts, local bodies, schools, coaches, families, and athletes.
questions.hint: The chapter lists those close to a young player's life.

questions.q: Which of these statements about policies of organisations is INCORRECT?
options: Schools, companies, hospitals, sports clubs, and even families often have their own policies
A school may have a policy on the use of mobile phones
A housing society may have rules for parking vehicles
Only governments can make policies
questions.explanation: Not just governments — schools, companies, hospitals, sports clubs, and even families make policies to guide the way they function. However, only policies made by governments for society at large are public policies.
questions.fact: Schools, companies, hospitals, sports clubs, and even families often have their own policies to guide the way they function.
questions.hint: Think of your school's own rules.

questions.q: Which of these statements about policy stakeholders is INCORRECT?
options: Elected representatives participate in law-making and approve budgets
Government officials prepare and implement policies and coordinate departments
International organisations bring international experience and financial support
Only ministers and government officials can contribute to policy-making
questions.explanation: Policy-making takes the combined efforts of many people — citizens, elected representatives, officials, civil society organisations, NGOs, the media, the private sector, and international organisations. Even ordinary citizens identify issues and provide solutions.
questions.fact: It takes the combined efforts of many individuals, organisations, officials, and even ordinary citizens in identifying issues, providing solutions, and putting them into action.
questions.hint: Remember the residents who requested a zebra crossing.

questions.q: Which of these statements about the NEP 2020 is INCORRECT?
options: Society changed rapidly over time, creating a need to rethink India's education system
The expert committee included experts from education, science, technology, social sciences, and public administration
The final policy was prepared after discussions within the Government of India
The National Education Policy 2020 was drafted without consulting any citizens or institutions
questions.explanation: NEP 2020 is the chapter's example of a collaborative policy: the draft was opened for public feedback, lakhs of local bodies were consulted, and about 2 lakh suggestions were received and examined before the final policy was prepared.
questions.fact: A unique feature of NEP 2020 was the large-scale public consultation. The draft policy was made available for feedback by citizens and all stakeholders.
questions.hint: The chapter calls NEP 2020 'a collaborative journey'.

questions.q: Which of these statements about the implementation of the Khelo Bharat Niti is INCORRECT?
options: The Khelo Bharat Niti mandates state governments to strengthen sporting ecosystems through initiatives such as 'Model Sports State'
Individual districts are encouraged to become 'Model Sports Districts' by enhancing their sports capabilities
State governments can attract private investments through the public-private partnership (PPP) model to build sports infrastructure
Blocks have no role to play in the Khelo Bharat Niti
questions.explanation: Blocks have a clear role: sporting programmes are organised there on a regular basis to attract mass participation and facilitate talent scouting. In fact, strengthening the ecosystem from the block level to the national level is the Niti's key focus.
questions.fact: Further at the level of blocks, sporting programmes are to be organised on a regular basis to attract mass participation and facilitate talent scouting.
questions.hint: The policy's focus begins at which level?

questions.q: Which of these statements about colonialism and governance is INCORRECT?
options: European powers colonised many societies, particularly those in Asia, Africa, and the Americas
Before colonial rule, these societies governed themselves in accordance with local and organic systems
India is an exception to the historical legacy of colonialism
Colonial rulers forced their own models of governance and policy-making on colonised people
questions.explanation: The chapter states that India is NOT an exception to the historical legacy of colonialism. However, India stands out for preserving pre-colonial traditions through texts and practices and for framing the Constitution in the spirit of India's own values.
questions.fact: India is not an exception to the historical legacy of colonialism.
questions.hint: India too inherited colonial institutions.

questions.q: Which of these statements about good governance is INCORRECT?
options: Good governance promotes justice and fairness
Good governance helps promote sustainable development and national progress
Good governance and public policy are crucial foundations for achieving national development goals
Good governance is a one-time achievement that requires no continued effort
questions.explanation: Good governance is an ongoing effort that helps realise the vision of making India a developed, prosperous, and self-reliant nation. It must be strengthened continuously as society's needs evolve.
questions.fact: Good governance is, therefore, an ongoing effort that will help realise the vision of making India a developed, prosperous, and self-reliant nation.
questions.hint: The chapter calls governance a task that is 'always ongoing'.

questions.q: Which of these statements about the hospital case study is INCORRECT?
options: Smt. Shanti Devi, a 72-year-old woman, found no ramp or handrail to reach the OPD
A man in a wheelchair was unable to enter the hospital building
After the improvements, the hospital became easier to use for older persons, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, patients, and children
The hospital building was already fully accessible, so no changes were needed
questions.explanation: The hospital was NOT accessible — there were no ramps, handrails, tactile pathways, or Braille signs. Only after the government funded ramps, lifts, handrails, tactile pathways, accessible toilets, and signboards did the building become easy to use for all.
questions.fact: The government approves the funds needed to construct ramps, lifts, handrails, tactile pathways, and accessible toilets, and to install clear signboards.
questions.hint: The whole case began because the building was hard to use.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Indian institutions have adapted traditional values of governance to the needs of a modern democracy.
Reason (R): Since Independence, these institutions have continued to draw upon traditional ideas and values of governance.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and R explains A: Indian institutions draw upon traditional ideas and values of governance and adapt them to the needs of a modern democracy, as seen in the adoption of 'Satyamev Jayate' and the honour given to the Sengol.
questions.fact: Since Independence, Indian institutions have continued to draw upon traditional ideas and values of governance and have adapted them to the needs of a modern democracy.
questions.hint: Tradition supplies the values; democracy supplies the setting.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The adoption of Indian mottos like 'Satyamev Jayate' after Independence is not just a symbolic or superficial change.
Reason (R): These mottos signify the core values and ideals of our institutions, along with the responsibility of ensuring good governance.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and R explains A: the chapter says such changes are not just symbolic because they signify the core values and ideals of our institutions, which carry the responsibility of ensuring good governance.
questions.fact: These changes are not just symbolic or superficial. They signify the core values as well as the ideals of our institutions, which have been bestowed along with the responsibility of ensuring good governance.
questions.hint: Ask why a motto matters beyond its words.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): For a policy to be implemented effectively, it is always further organised into programmes and schemes.
Reason (R): Programmes and schemes provide a clear framework for different ministries, departments, and local governments to take specific action.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and R explains A: once a policy is approved, it is translated into programmes and schemes that give ministries, departments, and local governments a clear framework for action.
questions.fact: Once the policy is approved by the concerned authorities, it is translated into programmes and schemes, which provide a clear framework for different ministries, departments, and local governments to take specific action.
questions.hint: Think about who actually carries out an approved policy.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The success of the Khelo Bharat Niti 2025 depends only on the Central Government.
Reason (R): The Union Government's role is primarily to provide the larger policy framework and funding for the Niti.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: A is false because the Niti's success depends on many stakeholders — states, districts, local bodies, schools, coaches, families, and athletes. R is true, as the Union Government mainly provides the policy framework and funding.
questions.fact: The government may plan a policy, but its success depends on many stakeholders — in this case, states, districts, local bodies, schools, coaches, families, and athletes.
questions.hint: Check whether one actor alone can deliver a national sports policy.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Under the Khelo Bharat Niti, the primary role of the Union Government is to host major national games and tournaments.
Reason (R): State governments are expected to host major national games and tournaments.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: A is false because hosting national games is the state governments' role, while the Union Government focuses on the larger policy framework and funding. R correctly states the states' expected role.
questions.fact: State governments are expected to host major national games and tournaments... the role of the Union Government is primarily focused on providing the larger policy framework.
questions.hint: Check which level of government does which job.
